ac-compressor-front-shaft-bearing.summary: A front radial shaft support is distinct from both the axial thrust stack and the clutch pulley bearing.
ac-compressor-front-shaft-bearing.limits: The single cartridge represents an unresolved support. Its 20 × 28 × 12 mm envelope and axial station are assumed around the study shaft; individual rolling elements, cage, races, tolerances and production identity are not established.

steps.title: Locate the shaft radially
steps.text: The bearing envelope lies between the rotating shaft and a stationary seat in the front cylinder half. Nominal touching surfaces illustrate where radial support is required, not a real running fit.

steps.title: Separate radial and axial support
steps.text: The manufacturer illustration labels the shaft bearing separately from the adjacent thrust-bearing and race stack. The latter addresses axial loading along the shaft.

steps.title: Do not confuse the pulley bearing
steps.text: The clutch pulley bearing surrounds the stationary front nose and lets the belt-side pulley rotate independently. It is not this internal shaft support.

ac-compressor-rear-shaft-bearing.summary: A second radial support locates the compressor shaft within the rear cylinder half.
ac-compressor-rear-shaft-bearing.limits: Only the comparison support count is sourced. Envelope dimensions, axial position, manufacturing fit and all bearing internals remain unresolved; no production or loaded-motion claim is made.

steps.title: Support the opposite shaft end
steps.text: The rear cartridge meets the study shaft and its own cylindrical seat. Its stationary envelope remains fixed while the shaft turns inside it.

steps.title: Keep the thrust stack separate
steps.text: The adjacent thrust races and rolling-element cartridge remain separate parts; the radial support does not replace them.

steps.title: Recognize the remaining evidence gap
steps.text: An identified bearing drawing or measured intact part is needed before splitting this envelope into real cups, rolling elements and cage geometry.
